issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

When creating an endpoint like this:

```csharp
    public IActionResult Get([FromQuery] Dictionary<string, string> test = null)
    {
        return Ok("test 123");
    }
```

The API call to succeed and return a value without crashing.

comments:
@tomer-amir Thanks for reporting this issue. I investigated the issue and this is caused by this change https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/830da4e50429f806c006d801545bac9874098a05. Basically, because we are not creating an empty collection when a default value is set, we missed an additional change to report the BindingResult to `IsModelSet = false`.

I will work on this and get back to you.

review_comments: Confirming my understanding here: this addresses the scenario where the model has been bound successfully and the user _did not_ provide `null` as a default value?
Yeah `model has been bound successfully` but in this case does not matter if it has a default value.  Of course, the default value will affect if the IsModelSet check before.

Am I correct that before .NET 7, given a`Get([FromQuery] Dictionary<string, string> test = null)` action and no "test"entries in the query string, you would get an empty collection instead of null? And in .NET 7 before this fix, you get a NullReferenceException before the action gets invoked?

If so, why didn't `CollectionModelBinder_DoesNotCreateEmptyCollection_IfModelHasDefaultValue` catch this? Do we need more end-to-end testing here? Are we going to backport this fix?

> Am I correct that before .NET 7, given aGet([FromQuery] Dictionary<string, string> test = null) action and no "test"entries in the query string, you would get an empty collection instead of null? And in .NET 7 before this fix, you get a NullReferenceException before the action gets invoked?

You are right.

> If so, why didn't CollectionModelBinder_DoesNotCreateEmptyCollection_IfModelHasDefaultValue catch this? Do we need more end-to-end testing here?

the problem is the `NullReference` happens in the `DictionaryBinder` that call the base.BindModelAsync (`CollectionModelBinder.BindModelAsync`) and was expecting a non-null IDictionary whe the `IsModelSet` is `true`.

This new test `DictionaryModelBinder_DoesNotCreateEmptyCollection_IfIsTopLevelObjectAndHasDefaultValue` would have caught this.

>  Are we going to backport this fix?

I believe we should.
